Summary

We are a one-of-a-kind, fully-funded, and global organization dedicated to empowering philanthropic leaders everywhere to take immediate and far-reaching climate action.
By serving as an impartial guide, we equip new climate philanthropists with the information, insights, and curated roadmaps needed to drive transformative climate solutions

We are seeking a strategic, highly capable Chief Operating Officer (COO)
to join our executive leadership team. Reporting directly to the President

In this pivotal role, you will lead day-to-day operations and coordinate across all key functional leaders to ensure seamless integration, operational excellence, and purpose alignment as the organization scales.

Managerial Responsibilities

The COO leads the organization's Operations, Legal, Finance, and Technology teams.
Direct Reports (5 FTE)
: Managing Director, Finance & Business Systems (Leadership Team member);Director of Operations; Interim Legal Counsel; Executive Assistant for Operations.
Indirect Reports (5.5 FTE)
: Director of Finance; Director of IT; Associate Director, Business Systems;Salesforce Administrator; Product Manager, Salesforce (0.5 FTE); Operations Coordinator.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

General Operations & Administration (40%)

Principal Operational Lead
: Oversee core administrative functions, contract management, facilities, and keyvendor relationships.
Planning & Alignment
: Lead organization-wide and cross-team priority setting and planning to removeoperational friction and foster a responsive operating environment.
Executive Strategy
: Partner with the Leadership Team on major organizational decisions affecting top-lineOKRs, strategy, and budget allocation.
Presidential Support
: Advise and support the President on operational strategies to expand and scaleengagement with key global partners.

Culture & Strategy
: Model organizational values and collaborate with the executive team to define long-termstrategic direction.
Fiduciary Responsibility

Finance & Business Systems (5%)

Operational Integration
: Enable the success of the MD, Finance & Business Systems across financialplanning, multi-year projections, IT systems, AI integration, and Salesforce administration.

Success Criteria

Values-Driven Executive
: Models authentic, values-led leadership, balancing high-level visionary strategywith practical, hands-on execution.
Diplomatic Partner
: Navigates complex multi-partner environments with diplomatic skill, building coalitionsacross functional and organizational boundaries.
Team Architect
: Designs operational structures that break down silos, promote cross-functional innovation,and cultivate organizational resilience.
Results-Oriented Operator
: Establishes operational feedback loops that connect daily execution directly tolong-term 2030 climate goals.
Functional Leader
: Synthesizes complex operational requirements into actionable organizational strategy,proactively identifying growth opportunities and removing blockers.

Qualifications

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Executive Management
: Outstanding leadership and team-building capability across operations, finance,technology, and legal functions.
Strategic & Tactical Agility
: Demonstrated ability to move effortlessly between overarching strategy andgranular, detailed tactical execution.
Contemporary Operations Toolkit

Entrepreneurial Rigor
: Combining the intellectual dynamism required for an entrepreneurial, fast-pacedenvironment with the discipline to build sustainable long-term infrastructure.

Education and Experience

Proven executive leadership track record (COO or senior operations lead) within high-growth, matrixed, orcomplex mission-driven organizations.
Demonstrated experience managing multi-disciplinary operational teams, supporting board governance, andoverseeing organizational risk.

Work Environment

Our organization is headquartered in San Francisco, CA, with additional staff hubs in London, New York, and Washington, D.C.
This position operates in a hybrid environment and is based in our San Francisco, CA office alongside the executive leadership team.
Staff based in the San Francisco Bay Area work in the office Tuesday through Thursday each week.

The actual salary offered will depend on various factors, including the candidate's level of directly relevant experience, core skills, and qualifications. This is a fixed compensation rate; the role does not include an annual bonus or carried interest.

jobs.description:
Position Overview

Generation Housing seeks a strategic, collaborative, and mission-driven Policy Director to lead the organization’s housing policy and advocacy efforts throughout Sonoma County and the North Bay.

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Policy Director directs Generation Housing’s on housing policy, land use, and housing production issues. The position is responsible for monitoring and analyzing local, regional, state, and federal policy developments; developing advocacy strategies and campaigns; building relationships with public officials and community partners; and helping shape Generation Housing's long-term policy agenda on issues including housing production, affordability, land use, transportation, and community development.
The Policy Director serves as a member of Generation Housing's leadership team, supervises the Policy Coordinator and plays a central role in shaping the organization's strategic direction.

This is a full-time (40 hours/week) exempt position.

Key Responsibilities

Political strategy and policy development (50%)

Direct and implement Generation Housing’s strategy on local, regional, state, and federal advocacy, policy positions, and campaigns that advance housing affordability, supply, and housing choice.
Monitor public meetings, legislation, budgets, General Plans, Housing Elements, housing production trends, and other policy developments relevant to Generation Housing’s mission.
Develop and implement advocacy strategies, policy positions, and campaigns that advance housing affordability, supply, and housing choice.
Conduct policy research and analysis to identify emerging opportunities and challenges and help develop annual advocacy priorities and work plans.
Provide strategic oversight and guidance to the Policy Coordinator's housing project monitoring, research, and endorsement activities.
Collaborate with staff and partners to build public support and political will for housing solutions.

Community relations and public leadership (25%)

Build and maintain productive relationships with elected and appointed policymakers, local government staff, housing developers and other stakeholders.
Facilitate Generation Housing’s Policy Committee and integrate member feedback into advocacy priorities
Coordinate regular engagement with housing and planning staff across Sonoma County jurisdictions.
Represent Generation Housing at public meetings, community events, and conferences, and develop educational content and programming, including workshops, trainings, and public presentations, to advance housing literacy and policy engagement. 

Research, communications and technical assistance (15%)

Oversee policy monitoring, research, and data analysis functions and translate findings into advocacy strategies and organizational priorities.
Prepare policy briefs, position papers, presentations, reports, public comments, and other written materials that position Generation Housing as a policy thought leader within the region.
Provide technical assistance and policy guidance to community members, partners, advocates, and local leaders.
Collaborate with staff to develop educational materials and public-facing communications. Operations, Management and Compliance (10%)
Supervise, mentor, and support the Policy Coordinator.
Develop work plans, establish priorities, and support staff professional development.
Assist with grant proposals, funder reporting, and program budget development
Track program activities and expenditures and maintain appropriate records.
Coordinate with the Executive Director, fiscal sponsor, legal counsel, and consultants regarding lobbying, advocacy, and compliance activities.
Contribute to organizational planning, fundraising, and other initiatives as needed.

Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

We recognize that candidates may not possess every qualification listed below. If you are excited about this role and believe you can contribute to Generation Housing's mission, we encourage you to apply. The ideal candidate will bring:
Experience developing and implementing policy, advocacy, public affairs, or political strategies.
Strong understanding of California housing policy, local governance, land use planning, and housing development, including Housing Elements, RHNA, housing streamlining laws, CEQA, and transit-oriented development. 
Demonstrated leadership experience, including personnel supervision, project management, and the ability to balance multiple in a dynamic environment.
Excellent written, verbal, and public speaking skills, including experience preparing reports, presentations, and educational materials.
Experience building relationships and working collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.
Strong strategic thinking, sound judgment, and the ability to navigate complex political environments.
Proficiency with Google Workspace, Zoom, Slack, and other cloud-based collaboration tools. 

Additional assets include:
Knowledge of Sonoma County or North Bay housing issues and stakeholders.
Experience with housing data analysis, GIS, Tableau, Airtable, R, Salesforce, or similar tools.
Experience facilitating workshops, trainings, or community engagement efforts.
Spanish language proficiency and/or bilingual and bicultural experience.
A master's degree in Public Policy, Urban Planning, Public Administration, Political Science, Sociology, or a related field is preferred but not required. Equivalent combinations of education and professional experience will be considered.

This position requires regular in-person engagement throughout Sonoma County, including meetings with local jurisdictions, elected officials, community partners, and attendance at public meetings. Candidates must reside within a reasonable commuting distance of Sonoma County or be willing to relocate upon hire.
Compensation

Salary for this position is $112,570-$123,826 annually.

Generation Housing utilizes a transparent compensation structure and does not negotiate salaries. This approach helps ensure consistency, fairness, and equity across our team. Additional compensation is available for qualifying credentials and skills, including Spanish language proficiency or fluency, master's degrees, and doctoral degrees.

As a project of the Tides Center, Generation Housing employees receive access to a comprehensive benefits package that is uncommon among organizations of our size.

Benefits include:

Comprehensive medical coverage for employees and dependents through Kaiser and Blue Shield plans, with Generation Housing covering nearly the full premium cost.
Dental, vision, life, AD&D, and disability insurance.
Maven family and reproductive health services.
FSA, HSA, commuter benefits, and Employee Assistance Program.
403(b) retirement plan with immediate vesting and employer match up to 5%.
Up to 25 vacation days, 12 wellness days annually, 12 paid holidays, and a floating holiday.
Paid parental leave and eligibility for Public Service Loan Forgiveness programs.

Generation Housing is committed to supporting employees as whole people. We strive to foster a workplace culture that values flexibility, professional growth, family responsibilities, and long-term sustainability while advancing meaningful work that improves communities throughout the North Bay.

Application

Please email a resume and cover letter to jobs@generationhousing.org and indicate “Policy Director – YOUR NAME” in the subject line of the email.

Relay Recruiting is proud to partner with a well-established nonprofit senior care and human services organization in the Rochester community, seeking a Director of Major Gifts to lead major and planned gift fundraising and deepen relationships with a loyal, multi-generational donor base.

The Opportunity

The Director of Major Gifts will step into a well-established portfolio of roughly 130–160 major gift and planned giving relationships, including several multi-generational family foundations, with warm introductions ready to go from day one. Reporting directly to the Foundation's Executive Director and working as part of the senior leadership team, this person will cultivate, solicit, and steward donors while also self-generating new prospects, particularly outside the organization's traditional donor community. Success in this role means blending relationship-driven stewardship with a disciplined process: building trust with donors and families who are often navigating long-term care, rehab, or memory care, while steadily growing gift size and building toward transformational giving. This is a role for a self-starter who thrives on process, enjoys working with a close-knit donor community, and wants a seat at the leadership table for a mission worth showing up for every day.

About the Company

This is a large, multi-service nonprofit serving older adults across independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing, rehabilitation, and memory care, with roughly 1,000 employees across its campus and programs. It's deeply rooted in community and tradition, with a culture that takes care of its employees, residents and their families. The foundation team is investing in its future, launching new signature fundraising events, growing its focus on donor cultivation beyond its traditional base, and renewing its push to engage the next generation of philanthropists. And with a supportive senior leadership team and strong internal relationships, it's a collaborative environment for someone ready to make a visible impact.

Key Responsibilities

Own and grow a well-established portfolio of major gift and planned giving donors, including numerous family foundations, picking up warm relationships from day one.
Cultivate, solicit, and steward major and planned gifts, building toward five- and six-figure asks with an eye toward transformational giving over time.
Proactively identify, research, and engage new major gift prospects, including donors outside the organization's traditional community, to diversify and grow the base.
Partner with the Executive Director to build and execute an annual major gift and planned giving work plan, including budgets, goals, and strategy.
Build relationships with estate and financial planning professionals, and guide donors and their advisors toward planned giving vehicles that meet shared goals.
Maintain current knowledge of gift and estate tax law and planned giving best practices.
Support grant writing and funder identification alongside the Executive Director, contributing to an annual portfolio of roughly a dozen grants.
Visit with donors and their families in long-term care, rehab, and memory care settings, communicating the Foundation's role with warmth and steadiness.
Represent the Foundation at community and donor events, including an annual golf tournament and emerging young-leader engagement efforts.
Deliver regular reporting and analysis on giving activity to the Foundation team and Board of Directors.

What We're Looking For

5+ years of progressive fundraising experience, with proven success in major gift and planned giving work.
A genuine self-starter who's comfortable building and working a prospect pipeline.
Bachelor's degree required.
Excellent relationship-building and stewardship instincts.
Comfort and compassion navigating conversations with families in long-term care, rehab, or memory care settings.
Experience with donor management systems (Raiser's Edge preferred).
Strong strategic planning, budgeting, and project management skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Bonus Points If You Have:

Grant writing or funder research experience.
A track record of growing a donor base into new or non-traditional communities.
Experience or interest in engaging next-generation or young donor audiences.

Compensation and benefits

Base salary $75K-$90K, commensurate with experience
Generous PTO package

Generation Housing seeks a strategic, collaborative, and mission-driven Policy Director to lead the organization’s housing policy and advocacy efforts throughout Sonoma County and the North Bay.

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Policy Director directs Generation Housing’s on housing policy, land use, and housing production issues. The position is responsible for monitoring and analyzing local, regional, state, and federal policy developments; developing advocacy strategies and campaigns; building relationships with public officials and community partners; and helping shape Generation Housing's long-term policy agenda on issues including housing production, affordability, land use, transportation, and community development.
The Policy Director serves as a member of Generation Housing's leadership team, supervises the Policy Coordinator and plays a central role in shaping the organization's strategic direction.

This is a full-time (40 hours/week) exempt position.

Key Responsibilities

Political strategy and policy development (50%)

Direct and implement Generation Housing’s strategy on local, regional, state, and federal advocacy, policy positions, and campaigns that advance housing affordability, supply, and housing choice.
Monitor public meetings, legislation, budgets, General Plans, Housing Elements, housing production trends, and other policy developments relevant to Generation Housing’s mission.
Develop and implement advocacy strategies, policy positions, and campaigns that advance housing affordability, supply, and housing choice.
Conduct policy research and analysis to identify emerging opportunities and challenges and help develop annual advocacy priorities and work plans.
Provide strategic oversight and guidance to the Policy Coordinator's housing project monitoring, research, and endorsement activities.
Collaborate with staff and partners to build public support and political will for housing solutions.

Community relations and public leadership (25%)

Build and maintain productive relationships with elected and appointed policymakers, local government staff, housing developers and other stakeholders.
Facilitate Generation Housing’s Policy Committee and integrate member feedback into advocacy priorities
Coordinate regular engagement with housing and planning staff across Sonoma County jurisdictions.
Represent Generation Housing at public meetings, community events, and conferences, and develop educational content and programming, including workshops, trainings, and public presentations, to advance housing literacy and policy engagement. 

Research, communications and technical assistance (15%)

Oversee policy monitoring, research, and data analysis functions and translate findings into advocacy strategies and organizational priorities.
Prepare policy briefs, position papers, presentations, reports, public comments, and other written materials that position Generation Housing as a policy thought leader within the region.
Provide technical assistance and policy guidance to community members, partners, advocates, and local leaders.
Collaborate with staff to develop educational materials and public-facing communications. Operations, Management and Compliance (10%)
Supervise, mentor, and support the Policy Coordinator.
Develop work plans, establish priorities, and support staff professional development.
Assist with grant proposals, funder reporting, and program budget development
Track program activities and expenditures and maintain appropriate records.
Coordinate with the Executive Director, fiscal sponsor, legal counsel, and consultants regarding lobbying, advocacy, and compliance activities.
Contribute to organizational planning, fundraising, and other initiatives as needed.

Other duties as assigned

Experience developing and implementing policy, advocacy, public affairs, or political strategies.

Demonstrated leadership experience, including personnel supervision, project management, and the ability to balance multiple in a dynamic environment.
Excellent written, verbal, and public speaking skills, including experience preparing reports, presentations, and educational materials.
Experience building relationships and working collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.
Strong strategic thinking, sound judgment, and the ability to navigate complex political environments.
Proficiency with Google Workspace, Zoom, Slack, and other cloud-based collaboration tools.

Knowledge of Sonoma County or North Bay housing issues and stakeholders.
Experience with housing data analysis, GIS, Tableau, Airtable, R, Salesforce, or similar tools.

Spanish language proficiency and/or bilingual and bicultural experience.

new_jobs.title: Director of Operations, New Content Experiences (NCX)
new_jobs.description:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

As the Director of Operations for New Content Experiences (NCX), you will be the operational architect behind the next era of Netflix entertainment. Operating in a high-impact 'start-up' environment within a global powerhouse, you will lead a multidisciplinary team tasked with bringing 0-to-1 experiences, including Live Events, Games, Podcasts, and emerging formats to life for millions of members. If you thrive on transforming abstract creative visions into scalable, flawless global launches, this is your opportunity to define the future of media consumption

You will lead a multifunctional team of Lead Program Managers, Creative Operations Program Managers, Launch Managers, and Launch Coordinators. Program Managers oversee the end-to-end program management required to stand up new experiences with our cross-functional partners in Content, Product Management, and Engineering teams, and to build and launch them on Netflix. Their work includes managing 0-1 new content roll-outs, overseeing the execution of new functionality and capabilities, facilitating the creation of product envelopes with our engineering partners, and ingesting and testing support of new content experiences as they come to the Netflix service. Launch Managers' seamless launches of all content on our Product, the implementation and execution of defined title merchandising strategies, operational solutions for bespoke positioning of our titles, and strong partnerships across our partners in the Content, Product, and Marketing teams. The Creative Operations team centralizes end-to-end gathering, distribution, and delivery of artifacts, context, and assets, and acts as the driving force in upholding creative production workflows within Product Merchandising.

As the leader of this multifunctional team, you should be comfortable in “start-up” mode and building high-profile 0–1 teams in new, emerging areas for the business. You will interface daily with executive leadership and cross-functional experts across Content, Game Studio, Content Ingestion & Distribution, Product Management, Engineering, Tech Operations, and Local Product Merchandising, vision brought to life by the Experience Design team and the real-life content deals that arrive on our doorstep at a rapid pace.

In This Role, You Will Be Responsible For

Scale the Future: Architect and oversee clear workflows and documentation (playbooks, onboarding materials, presentations) to rapidly and consistently “graduate” new content experiences to be operationalized by our regional product merchandising teams. Continue to set the standard for excellence, pioneering innovations for New Content Experiences before rolling them out globally.
Constantly work to scale and simplify the intake, operationalization, and contingency planning processes for new content experiences. Continuously pressure test and streamline workflows to ensure optimized speed to launch, risk management, and opportunities for enhancements.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Serve as the critical bridge between Content, Engineering, Product Management, and Experience Design, translating complex content deals into clear operational workflows and technical roadmaps.
Drive Launch Excellence: Oversee risk management, SLAs, and contingency planning to ensure flawless execution during high-stakes, time-sensitive critical launch windows (e.g., Live streams).
Develop Top Talent: Mentor and grow a world-class multidisciplinary team of Program Managers, Launch Managers, and Creative Operations specialists, fostering a culture of innovation, speed, and continuous improvement.
Hands-on Execution & Global Scaling: Act as a "player-coach" who is willing to personally drive highly ambiguous, high-profile launches, while simultaneously building the playbooks necessary to "graduate" these workflows to regional merchandising teams worldwide. Ensure constant strategic alignment by providing synthesized, high-level visibility to executive leadership.
Maintain strong partnerships with Regional Product merchandising leaders to help tether local content experience to the evolution of the product and product leaders.

Qualifications

Extensive leadership experience building and managing multidisciplinary operations or program management teams, ideally within complex product, media, or tech environments.
Proven track record of operating in '0-to-1' spaces, bringing structure, alignment, and scale to highly ambiguous, fast-paced initiatives.
Exceptional executive communication skills, with the ability to distill complex operational realities into clear memos and presentations for C-level leadership. Proven ability to influence matrixed cross-functional partners (Engineering, Content, Product) without direct authority.
A data-informed operational mindset; comfortable using both quantitative and qualitative methods to identify workflow bottlenecks and pioneer new solutions.
An insatiable curiosity for the evolving media landscape (Live, Games, emerging formats), coupled with a deep empathy for diverse global regions to ensure workflows scale seamlessly across international markets.
